title: Fanboyism is a mental illness: How Youtubers steal your identity through parasocial relationships
summary: A 100-minute monologue defining fanboyism as a mental illness created by parasocial relationships, and explaining how fitness channels turn into cult-like groups that worship the creator, attack dissenters and strip viewers of identity. He urges viewers to trust themselves, disagree openly, train instead of watching, and ends by ranking the worst fanboy communities and commenter types on YouTube fitness.
claims: Fanboyism is a mental illness built through parasocial relationships; it makes the fan and the people around him miserable
Fanboyism is idolizing someone other than yourself and surrendering your identity to a perceived group; you lose agency and become passive
When nut-huggers outnumber critical thinkers in a group, idolization becomes the norm and is aggressively defended; this happens to every channel as it grows
Morals are not abstract; a moral exists only as long as enough people keep applying it
Do not call yourself a fan (from fanatical); language dictates action, and calling yourself a fan teaches you to be subservient
Celebrity worship is selfish: people worship hoping to become their idol, and the hidden hatred they feel toward someone they aspire to be is really self-hatred
A parasocial relationship is a one-sided bond built through media with a person of influence; YouTube puts creator and viewer on unequal footing by default, an evolutionary mismatch
No one on YouTube fitness is your friend; Natural Hypertrophy is an avatar, and the healthiest way to consume any content is to see through the person
Loyalty is for your family and your dog, not YouTubers; take what you can get from a channel and leave
Constant positivity links a creator to your dopamine receptors; he stays brutally honest and likes offending viewers because it breaks the parasocial bond
Disagreement is key: if you agree with 100% of what he says, you are either too green to know better or the parasocial bond has set in
Watch videos for your own benefit, not the creator's; never apologize for not watching or not liking a video
Fanboyism can be more damaging long-term than anxiety or depression and harder to cure, because it removes the ability to notice you are being hurt
Whether a lifting journey succeeds and lasts depends on forming your own connection with lifting, more than on optimal gains, bulking vs cutting, or program choice
He discovered lifting by himself, curling chairs, lifting rocks and sprinting in the mountains; gains were not optimal but it built his own identity
Confidence comes from inside; if your belief in natural lifting rests on a YouTuber, it shatters the day he admits he lied or took steroids
Results justify effort, but results take time; comparing yourself to someone 15 times your size with 10 years of training kills drive, so only your own progression matters
Doing repeated favors for someone makes you like them; similarly an audience that keeps listening to a creator concludes he must be superior
Inside jokes built on a creator's repeated traits turn into meaningless mantras that new members repeat without understanding
Fanboys react aggressively to criticism of their idol because their identity is the group, so criticism of him feels like an attack on themselves
On Greg Doucette's channel the 'I'm not a doctor' joke devolved into fans calling him their doctor, therapist and dad: a slide from mockery to worship
Post a timestamped critique on any big fitness channel and the creator will ignore it while commenters insult you instead of arguing
When joking about the creator starts getting hostile reactions, the channel has been taken over by fanboys and he leaves
Hyperbolic worship comments justify the time fans invest and, like writing a goal down, crystallize and spread fanboyism
A creator publicly banning dissenters reinforces the parasocial bond and teaches fans it is fine to go after people who disagree
Most YouTube viewers are under 20 and lack a formed identity, so a creator can replace their core; novices likewise cannot judge whether information is good
Do not trust him, trust yourself; if you cannot evaluate what a YouTuber says, step away and build your own knowledge base before returning
A channel's purpose should be to produce individuals; there is no fanboy with a great physique because fanboys lose the ability to develop themselves
Hype watching: people click a video with 80,000 views over the identical one with 80; channel size has no correlation with information quality
The halo effect makes people with attractive bodies seem more knowledgeable, and bigger crowds strengthen it
Parasocial relief keeps lonely people from going out and forming real relationships
Many people long for spirituality but reject it because they confuse it with religion, which he sees as politics
Fame destroys big YouTubers: the audience molds them into a flanderized meme of themselves, and chasing numbers, like steroid cycles, never satisfies
Testimony comments credit the YouTuber, but if you lost 80 pounds you did it, not him
Vlogs, face cams, faces in thumbnails, merch, Discords, expos and community polls all feed the parasocial; he refuses to start a Discord for that reason
Mukbang videos fill the void of the social meal in a lonely society
Too many people watch training videos without training; spending more time on YouTube fitness than training is unacceptable, go do push-ups
Jumping from an exposed guru to the new savior who exposed him is an abusive cycle; leave it, only you can save yourself
Deciding to trust no one means you no longer trust your own judgment; trust yourself instead
Disagree openly, without the deferential 'respectfully' and without pre-emptive aggression, which becomes a self-fulfilling prophecy
Always ask how something benefits you; the group needs you, not the other way around
Worst fanboys: Eric Bugenhagen's subscribers, whose ironic worship became serious and includes strength copers who resent aesthetics and accuse him of not being natural
Greg Doucette's audience embodies hype watching, and Athlean-X is too big to fail and targets the fresh Indian novice market
A marketing scheme aimed only at people not strong enough to protect themselves is a scam every time
